etymologies.etymologyHTML: 14c. "credit, good reputation", Latin reputationem (“consideration, thinking over”), noun of action from past participle stem of reputo (“reflect upon, reckon, count over”), from the prefix re- (“again”) + puto (“reckon, consider”). Displaced native Old English hlīsa, which was also the word for "fame."

definitions.definition: What somebody or something is known for.

quote.citation: 1529, John Frith, A pistle to the Christen reader. The Revelation of Antichrist: Antithesis,  […] ‎[1], Luft [i.e. Hoochstraten], page 117:
quote.text: And Balaam (or as the trueth of the hebrewe hath Bileam) doth signifie the people of no reputation / or the vayne people or they that are not counted for people.

quote.citation: 1928, Franklin D. Roosevelt, The Happy Warrior Alfred E. Smith‎[2], Houghton Mifflin, →OCLC, page 12:
quote.text: Sometimes a man makes a reputation, deserved or otherwise, by a single action.
